function: TD-DDPG agent selects the RIS phase shifts (transmit power follows from a closed-form rule) to maximize the received SNR, which maximizes the AoI-driven effective capacity (pp. 6-7).
system: Reflecting-only RIS with F=30 elements between source S and destination D (antenna counts not stated), Rician links, short packets, 180 kHz bandwidth, carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 9).
method: Twin delayed DDPG (actor, two critics, clipped double Q-learning, delayed policy updates, target smoothing); reinforcement learning with reward equal to the received SNR (pp. 7-8).
data_channel: No dataset: simulated environment; Rician S-RIS and RIS-D links (K=10), distance path loss, LoS array response, parameters in Table II (pp. 3, 9).
test_conditions: Reward curve over 800 episodes (Fig. 4); results swept over RIS elements F=10-30, AoI threshold, packet size, QoS exponent, power; no separate test conditions stated (pp. 9-11).
baselines: Non-learned: random RIS phase shift and no RIS. Learned: DDPG-based phase shift ([26], [30]); same power rule for all schemes (p. 9).
metrics: AoI-driven effective capacity (BPCU), overall error probability, reward convergence over episodes, running time (pp. 9-11).
complexity: Multiplication-count complexity over actor and critic layer sizes (formula given); average running time 16.8 ms on AMD Ryzen 7 5800H (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 3: "the S-RIS channel and the RIS-D channel experience the Rician fading"; a custom Rician model with path loss PL(d) and LoS array response, not 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "Fig. 5 shows the effective capacity obtained by the four schemes for the different F"; F is swept, but the paper never states that an agent trained at one setting is tested at another, nor any fine-tuning or transfer.
q3_support: p. 9: "the proposed scheme is better than the DDPG-based scheme (with the gap of 25.1%) and the no RIS scheme and the random scheme", in effective capacity; DDPG baseline cited as [26], [30].
q4_support: p. 11: "The average running time of TD-DDPG-based algorithm is 16.8ms"; the same section gives the complexity order from actor and critic layer dimensions.
q5_support: p. 9: "Table II lists the other simulation setting parameters"; parameters only, no code or data link or DOI, a simulated channel, and no public dataset or measurement.
notes: Included as area 3: the agent learns the RIS phase shifts and the power follows from Eq. 28 (pp. 6-7). The target is a cross-layer QoS metric (AoI-driven effective capacity), but the learned decision is physical layer with SNR reward, so above_phy does not apply; a RIS is present, so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply. DDPG is the predecessor of TD-DDPG but is a standard algorithm applied to the same problem and cited from earlier works, so it counts as the learned baseline. Table II, Fig. 3 and the complexity formula were read from PDF pages 7, 9 and 11.
